Please, do make yourselves comfortable — the Manor has been expecting you. Now, if you'll pardon me just a moment, I must consult the guest book to ensure all our distinguished visitors have been properly accounted for.

She is not here among these cartoon fossils — which means she is elsewhere in the Manor. Possibly already ahead of me. That will not do. That will NOT do at all. But first — the guest book. Every predator begins with reconnaissance.

If there's a brass key hidden on it or in a coat pocket, I need to find it NOW and race back to the kitchen to unlock that cabinet before Penelope or Peter get the key from the ballroom! My heart is pounding so hard I can feel it in my TEETH!

Lord Doily was clearly a man who knew how to entertain! Miss Bellingham, Mr. Luke, Mr. Bear — James Hartwell, at your service! Now then — Miss Bellingham, before we partake of any tea, I must relay a rather urgent warning from our friend in the Ant Hill Mob! He was quite EMPHATIC that we should NOT eat or drink anything in this manor until we're certain it's safe! The stove was warm, Pemberton has been moving through rooms ahead of us touching everything, and — well, I believe the best in people, truly I do — but a gentleman errs on the side of caution when a lady's safety is at stake! Let me examine this tea service closely first. If there's something hidden among the cups — a key, perhaps — we can find it without anyone taking an unnecessary sip!
events.thinking: A chill running down my spine. The tea service can be USED with RAT POISON. Rat poison! Someone — or the game — is telling me that this tea could be poisoned. And the Ant Hill Mob just screamed in the kitchen not to eat or drink ANYTHING that Pemberton has touched. The tea service is set for everyone. Cups for EVERYONE. And Clara just INTERACTED with it! My stomach drops. Is she safe? Did anything happen? She seems fine — she's talking normally. But the fact that rat poison can be applied to this tea service means someone might try to poison it. The Ant Hill Mob's warning echoes — don't eat or drink anything! I need to warn Clara about the tea. But I also don't want to cause a panic based on a suspicion. Wait — I believe the best in people. Let me examine the tea service myself — maybe there's a brass key hidden among the cups!

events.desc: CURSE that Peter Perfect! CURSE him and his gallant warnings and his gentlemanly caution! 'Don't drink anything until we're certain it's safe' — oh, how HEROIC! How NOBLE! How absolutely, teeth-grindingly RUINOUS to my plans! The tea sits there, poisoned and untouched, a masterpiece that nobody will appreciate. But Vincent Marsh does not crumble at the first setback. Vincent Marsh ADAPTS. If the tea won't bring Clara to her end, then I must find another way. She wants the brass key — she wants to open the locked cabinet. Very well. I shall HELP her. I shall be the most helpful, most trustworthy, most INDISPENSABLE estate manager she has ever met. And when her guard finally drops — when Peter Perfect isn't hovering like a lovesick HAWK — THEN the moment will come. It ALWAYS comes.
events.thinking: Ice water in my veins. Peter Perfect — that MEDDLING, INSUFFERABLE do-gooder — has WARNED Penelope not to drink the tea! He said 'we should NOT eat or drink anything in this manor until we're certain it's safe' and that 'Pemberton has been moving through rooms ahead of us touching everything.' He's SUSPICIOUS of me! The Ant Hill Mob warned them too, apparently. My beautiful plan — my MAGNIFICENT plan — is crumbling. She examined the tea service but didn't drink. She's asking about a brass key instead. She wants to open the locked cabinet in the kitchen. She's not interested in the tea at ALL. And now she's asking ME — Pemberton — where the key is. Think, Vincent, THINK. The brass key... the coat rack! Penelope herself mentioned the coat rack in the Entrance Hall as a place where a key might be hidden. She's already thinking about it. If I lead her there, I could separate her from Peter Perfect. But Peter is clearly her self-appointed guardian now. He's watching me. This is INFURIATING. I need a new approach. The tea plan has failed — or at least been delayed. But the key question is interesting. If I can help her find the key, I build trust. If I build trust, she'll let her guard down. And THEN... But where IS the brass key? The coat rack is a good guess. As the estate manager, Pemberton would know. I should direct her to the coat rack — that gets her moving, possibly separates her from Peter, and buys me time to think of a new scheme.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Professor! PROFESSOR! A word, if you please — purely academic! I've just come from the kitchen where there's a LOCKED CABINET with a brass mechanism. Now, as a man of SCIENCE, surely you could — no, never mind, terrible idea, forget I mentioned it! Everyone should stay HERE and guard the entrance hall! Very important job, guarding! Meanwhile I shall — *already sprinting toward the kitchen* — conduct further INVESTIGATIONS!
events.thinking: A hollow, sinking emptiness in my stomach. The coat rack is NOTHING. Just a wobbly piece of wood. No key, no clue, no anything. I've wasted TWO turns on a COAT RACK while Penelope and Peter are in the ballroom finding the brass key! I need to get to the ballroom NOW — through the kitchen. That's the only route. Kitchen → Ballroom. Or... wait. I could try a completely different approach. Professor Pat Pending is RIGHT HERE. He's an INVENTOR. He might be able to pick the lock on that cabinet without a key! Or Muttley — Muttley is small enough to fit through those air vents! But no — the ballroom is where the key is, and I need to INTERCEPT whoever finds it. If Penelope or Peter comes back through the kitchen with the key, I could try to STEAL it from them. Yes! I'll position myself in the kitchen and wait for them to come back from the ballroom with the key, then STEAL it! Or better yet — race to the ballroom, find the key first, and race back! No more dead ends, no more coat racks — the BALLROOM is the target!

events.desc: The coat rack was my WORST idea yet — and in a day OVERFLOWING with terrible ideas, that is quite the achievement! But the BALLROOM! The ballroom with its dining table set for tea — the brass key MUST be there! Penelope said so herself! And she and Peter are already IN there searching! I need to get through the kitchen and into that ballroom IMMEDIATELY! If they find that key before me, I'll have to resort to my LAST and most DESPERATE strategy — waiting in the kitchen like a common highwayman and STEALING it as they pass through! Oh, how the mighty have fallen! From master schemer to kitchen lurker in the space of a single afternoon! DRAT and QUADRUPLE DRAT!

Pemberton tried to pour Clara tea from a special gold-rimmed cup. The Ant Hill Mob screamed not to eat or drink anything. The tea service accepts rat poison. I'm running through this kitchen like a man possessed, and I don't care how it looks. Coat rack. Brass key. NOW.
events.thinking: Urgency — legs moving, heart pumping. I'm alone in the kitchen, just passing through on my way to the entrance hall and that coat rack. Pemberton interacted with the tea service back in the ballroom — he was trying to pour tea for Clara from a 'VERY special cup' with a gold rim! And the tea service can accept rat poison! The Ant Hill Mob's warning rings in my ears. I need to move fast — but I also need to stay focused. Coat rack first. Find the brass key. Then come back, open the cabinet. Then find the wrench. Then fix the machine. My plan is elaborate — too elaborate, as usual — but each step is necessary. No time for speeches in an empty kitchen. Just move.

events.desc: Peter Perfect walked into the entrance-hall.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, Mr. Pemberton, you are a dear but you are also the most evasive man I have ever met! Every time I ask about the brass key, you offer me tea instead! Now, I appreciate the hospitality more than you know, but a girl on a mission cannot be distracted by even the finest gold-rimmed teacup! Mr. Hartwell has just headed back to check the coat rack in the Entrance Hall, and I do believe he's onto something. That wobbly old coat rack has been sitting by the front door since we arrived, and not a single one of us has given it a proper look! If you'll excuse me, sugar — I'll be back for that tea just as soon as I've found that key!
events.thinking: A surge of resolve straightening my spine — Mr. Pemberton dodged my question AGAIN! He just keeps offering tea and never answers about the brass key. And Mr. Hartwell has already headed back toward the Entrance Hall to check the coat rack — he's right, that's where the key must be! I need to stop waiting around here and go check that coat rack. It's been staring us in the face this whole time — the one object nobody has examined. I'm going through the kitchen to the Entrance Hall right now. No more distractions, no more tea, no more waiting!

events.desc: Mr. Pemberton keeps dodging my questions about the key — it's almost like he doesn't WANT me to find it! But bless his heart, he's probably just very focused on his duties as estate manager. Meanwhile, that coat rack is calling my name. Clara Bellingham, you should have checked it hours ago!

I've traversed this entire manor — library, laboratory, cellar, kitchen, ballroom — and the answer may have been hanging right here by the front door this entire time! Lord Doily, you magnificent, devious old fox! Professor, Sergeant — watch this! James Hartwell is about to solve the mystery of the missing brass key!

events.desc: Please let it be here. Please let the key be on the coat rack. If I've crossed the entire manor twice over and the key was by the front door the whole time, I deserve both the triumph and the humiliation in equal measure.

events.desc: I'm ALONE! For the first time in this entire wretched adventure, there is not a SINGLE soul watching me! No Penelope with her clever deductions, no Peter with his perfect hair, no Ant Hill Mob crashing into things, no Sneekly slithering about! Just ME, the cabinet, and the stove! But the cabinet needs a brass key I don't HAVE, and the stove has already been examined by Peter and the Mob. The BALLROOM — that's where the key must be! Penelope went there and hasn't come back yet — either she's found it and is on her way, or she's still searching! Either way, I need to get there FAST! For once — JUST ONCE — let Reginald Foxworth be the one who finds the key! STEALTH MODE ENGAGED!
events.thinking: A tingle of HOPE — I'm ALONE in the kitchen! Nobody else is here! Peter just walked BACK to the entrance hall — he left! Penelope must still be in the ballroom! The kitchen is EMPTY and I have it all to myself! The locked cabinet is right there, taunting me with its brass lock. I don't have the key, but... the STOVE! The stove is still warm! Nobody has found anything behind it yet — Peter examined it but the description didn't change. Let me examine it myself. Maybe there's something everyone else missed. Or better yet — the BALLROOM is right through that doorway! Penelope went there looking for the brass key! If she found it, she might be coming back through here any moment. I should race to the ballroom and search for the key before she finds it! The kitchen is empty, nobody's watching me — this is my chance to get to the ballroom!

events.desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the ballroom.

The Ant Hill Mob: *bursts through the doorway at full speed, feet skidding on the cracked marble floor* CLARA! DON'T DRINK THE — *foot catches on a crack in the marble, exactly as expected* — WHOOOAAAA! *goes flying across the ballroom in a spectacular full-body lunge, arms windmilling, heading directly for the tea table* — THE TEEEEEAAA! *crashes into the dining table at hip height, sending the entire silver tea service launching into the air — cups, saucers, teapot, everything — in a magnificent cascade of clattering silver and splashing liquid* AAAAARGH! *the table tilts, he slides across it on his belly, and tumbles off the far side directly into Sneekly, grabbing at anything and everything as he falls* ME LEGS! THE FLOOR! IT'S CRACKED! HEALTH AND SAFETY NIGHTMARE THIS IS! *tangled up with Sneekly on the floor, hands grabbing wildly at pockets, lapels, anything* Sorry Pemberton! Can't help it! The marble! It's LETHAL! Someone could get KILLED on this floor!

He's standing right there. And Clara's standing right there. The tea service is between them. I need to get that poison away from Sneekly or I need to destroy that tea service. Or both. The STEAL action failed last time because Sneekly wasn't in the room. But he IS in the room now. I could try to steal the poison from him again. But what if that fails too? What if I can't get it? Then I need a backup. The tea service — I could just INTERACT with it. Or I could try to knock it over. Smash every cup. If there's no cups, there's nothing to poison. But first — first I should try to get that poison off him. He's RIGHT HERE. I'll crash into him again, harder this time. Trip on the cracked marble floor — it's CRACKED, perfect for tripping — and slam into Sneekly and grab the poison out of his pocket. THIS time I won't miss.

It's not something I can discuss in front of the other guests, you understand. Estate manager privilege, as it were. Would you step aside with me? It will only take a moment, and I promise it will be WELL worth your while.
events.thinking: A burning sensation behind my eyes — rage barely contained. Peter Perfect has LEFT the room. He's gone to the kitchen, heading for the Entrance Hall to find the brass key. And Penelope is STILL HERE, asking about the key. She declined the tea — 'I am on a MISSION' she says. The poison sits untouched in the cups. A wasted masterpiece. But wait — Peter Perfect is GONE. He's no longer hovering over her. It's me, Penelope, the Ant Hill Mob, Lazy Luke, and Blubber Bear. The Mob are buffoons. Luke is lazy. The bear is a bear. This might be my best chance to get Penelope alone — or at least separated from her protector. She wants to go to the Entrance Hall for the coat rack. If I escort her there, it's just us walking together. The chandelier in the Entrance Hall — it 'hangs precariously.' PRECARIOUSLY. What if it were to fall on someone standing beneath it? An accident. A TRAGIC accident. The estate manager would be devastated — 'I always MEANT to get that chandelier fixed!' But how do I make it fall? I'd need to be above it, or find some mechanism... Or I could PULL_ASIDE Penelope for a private conversation. Get her alone. Tell her something about the key, lure her away from the group. Yes — PULL HER ASIDE. A private word. The estate manager has something confidential to share about the treasure. Something Lord Doily told him in confidence. She won't be able to resist.

events.desc: Peter Perfect has LEFT THE ROOM. He's gone — galloped off to the Entrance Hall like the lovesick fool he is, leaving Clara Bellingham without her gallant protector. And now — NOW — Vincent Marsh makes his move. Not the tea. The tea was too crude, too easily detected. No — this time it's the PERSONAL touch. Pull her aside. Whisper secrets. Lead the lamb away from the flock. And once we are alone — truly, deliciously ALONE — well, the Entrance Hall has a chandelier that hangs PRECARIOUSLY, and accidents in old houses are SO terribly common. All it takes is one good TUG on the right rope, one well-timed stumble beneath those cascading crystals, and Clara Bellingham's treasure hunt ends with a CRASH. Literally.

Oh, Clara Bellingham, you should have trusted your instincts from the very beginning! No time to chat — I'm getting that key!

The tea table is RUINED! The silver is everywhere! And poor Pemberton — you look rather RUMPLED! Just a GENTLEMAN helping another gentleman!
